IGN — BD TOPO®, vine zones (zone de végétation « Vigne »)
BRGM — Cartes géologiques harmonisées à 1/50 000 (BD Charm-50)
INRAE — Carte des sols de France (soil types, via IGN Géoplateforme)
BIVB — La Bourgogne et ses appellations (level of each appellation: Grand Cru, village, regional)
sources.licence: Reference list, no open licence stated

truthBoundary: Vineyard land is the vine cover mapped by IGN in BD TOPO, not the INAO parcel delimitation of the appellations.

Which appellations are Grand Cru, village or regional comes from the BIVB list (INAO publishes no such field): names it lists as sub-entries (the Mâcon villages, the "Bourgogne + area" names) take the level of the entry they sit under, and a name it does not list counts as village level.

Appellations come from the INAO parcel delimitation (informational; the official plan is the one filed at the town hall or with INAO, and not every AOC is digitised). It is cut to the mapped vines. A cadastral lieu-dit is not an appellation: it takes the tier covering most of it, and where under half of it lies on delimited parcels the old name matching (INAO climat name to lieu-dit name) is used and is approximate.
Lieux-dits not matched to a listed climat take their commune’s base level (Village, or Regional for communes with only regional appellations).
Surface geology is the rock unit mapped at 1:50 000 under the plot, not the soil. Where the legend states no stage, age is inferred from the unit’s name, code or kind (marked ≈) or left blank.
Weather is a modelled reanalysis for the surrounding ≈9–25 km area, not a measurement on the plot; GDD base 10 °C, ET₀ FAO-56, climate type from 1991–2020 monthly normals.
Soil type is the dominant type mapped by INRAE at regional scale where the plot lies, not a measurement on the plot.
